item.title: Sharp Signed Mass and Rigidity for Critical Finsler--Liouville Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study bounded-above entire solutions of critical Finsler--Liouville equations with a possibly sign-changing prescribed function and finite absolute mass. Under a lower cone-growth condition, we establish a sharp signed-mass bound without upper growth or monotonicity assumptions. With an additional growth condition, annular compactness for a sequence of dilations yields Pohozaev boundary limits and rigidity for radially nonincreasing prescribed functions. Explicit examples show that the rigidity threshold is optimal. In the Euclidean plane, the mass estimate also gives a sharp obstruction to completeness.
item.dc:creator: Yanjun Liu, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang

item.title: A Critical Case for the Near Field Refraction Problem in Negative Refractive Index Material
item.description: arXiv:2610.26998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the near field refraction problem for the critical case in negative refractive index material. Snell law in vector form is first reviewed, and the physical constraint governing refraction is discussed. We then define the refractor for the critical case and analyze several of its key properties. Building on these properties, we introduce the notion of a weak solution to this problem and prove the existence of the weak solution when the target measure is either discrete or a finite Radon measure. The proof relies on the Minkowski method, an iterative approach to refraction and reflection problems in geometric optics.
item.dc:creator: Yi He, Feida Jiang, Haokun Sui

item.title: A Brezis--Merle inequality for the biharmonic operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions in four-dimensional balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.27212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a Brezis-Merle type inequality for very weak solutions of the biharmonic Dirichlet problem in the four-dimensional unit ball. By combining this inequality with moving-plane arguments, we obtain uniform a priori estimates for positive solutions of semilinear biharmonic equations with exponential nonlinearities in both the subcritical and critical regimes. As an application of these estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of topological methods. We also extend the analysis to a class of non-variational cooperative systems.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Federica Sani, Victor Rafael Silva

item.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.27218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.
item.dc:creator: Ihsan Topaloglu

item.title: Explicit sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality and fundamental gaps for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.27281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality with explicit constants on bounded convex domains for any $1<p<\infty$. These estimates control the distance to the optimizers in the strongest possible norm with the optimal stability exponent $\max\{2,p\}$, exhibiting the same phenomenon initially observed by Figalli and Zhang [FZ22a] for the $L^p$-Sobolev inequality. As a result, we also confirm the conjecture posed by Fleckinger-Pell\'e and Tak\'a\v{c} [FPT02, Section 8]. We then apply the inequality to obtain positive fundamental gap estimates in terms of the inradius for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Nurgissa Yessirkegenov, Amir Zhangirbayev

item.title: Monomial Moving Zeros for the Heat Semigroup: An Explicit Finite-Order Differential Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.27326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P_t=\exp(t\D^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup. For every integer $k\geq2$ and parameter $\rho\in\C$, we construct an entire function $\Gamma_{\rho,k}$ whose heat evolution has the prescribed moving zero $x=\rho t^k$ and constant spatial flux there: \[ (P_t\Gamma_{\rho,k})(\rho t^k)=0, \qquad \partial_x(P_t\Gamma_{\rho,k})(\rho t^k)=1. \] The initial function is explicit, \[ \Gamma_{\rho,k}(x) =x\sum_{q\geq0}\frac{(-2^k\rho x^{2k-1})^q}{q!} \frac{(kq)!}{((2k-1)q+1)!}, \] and is a generalized hypergeometric function whose entire-function order is strictly below two. Most importantly, it is annihilated by an explicit polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2k-1$. Thus every monomial moving boundary admits a finite-order stationary realization after a natural boundary-flux selection, even though the naive order-$k$ family $\D^k+a x^{k-1}$ already fails to produce the exact boundary at $k=4$. No minimality claim is made: the result gives a universal finite-order hierarchy, while the least possible differential order remains open and depends on the choice made inside the inverse kernel.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Hernandez-del-Valle

item.title: Optimal global well-posedness for semilinear heat equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the question of global in time existence for the semilinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} \partial_t u-\Delta u&=&|u|^{b-1}u \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n\times (0,\infty),\\ u(\cdot,0)&=& u_0 \quad {\rm ~in~} \mathbb{R}^n, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $b> 1+2/n, n\geq 1$. We found a space of initial data $Z$ that guarantees the existence of a global in time solution whenever the norm of the initial datum $u_0$ in $Z$ is small. The space $Z$ is optimal in the sense that if $u_0$ is a nonnegative distribution and the equation admits a nonnegative solution $u\in L^b_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty))$, then $u_0\in Z$. Moreover, our result contains all of the known results in the literature. In particular, it implies that global in time existence does hold for end-point Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, which resolves an open problem posed by L. Brandolese and F. Cortez (J. Funct. Anal. $\textbf{276}$ (2019), 2589-2604).
item.dc:creator: Gael Y. Diebou, Nguyen Cong Phuc

item.title: The Inverse Problem of Velocity Reconstruction from Flow-Induced Magnetic Fields: Stability and Uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2610.27409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconstruction of velocity fields from flow-induced magnetic measurements is a fundamental inverse problem in magnetohydrodynamics, with broad applications in geophysics, astrophysics, and metallurgy. To address the nonlinearity of the governing equations, the magnetic induction equation is linearized around a known, space-dependent background magnetic field. This reveals a coupled parabolic--hyperbolic system in which magnetic diffusion interacts with velocity advection along the background field lines. By decoupling these mechanisms into a two-stage framework, sufficient conditions are established for both the uniqueness and stability of the velocity recovery. The main result proves that the non-uniqueness arising from unobservable velocity perturbations parallel to the background field is eliminated when the velocity trace on the inflow boundary is prescribed alongside magnetic observations. The analysis yields global uniqueness and a quantitative stability estimate of hybrid type: a Lipschitz contribution from the inflow trace combined with a weaker modulus from the parabolic observation, reflecting the mixed parabolic--hyperbolic structure of the problem. These theoretical findings are validated through three-dimensional numerical simulations that demonstrate the robustness of the decoupled reconstruction approach under noisy conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yacine Mokhtari

item.title: Schauder estimates for quasilinear parabolic equations with general Orlicz growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.27426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified approach to Schauder estimates for scalar parabolic equations \[ \partial_t u-\operatorname{div}\big(\mathcal{A}(x,t,Du)\big)=f(x,t) \] with general Orlicz growth and coefficients that are H\"older continuous in the spatial variables and merely measurable in time. Combining intrinsic gradient estimates with a perturbative argument, we establish quantitative local bounds and H\"older estimates for the spatial gradient in the supercritical range and, for locally bounded weak solutions, throughout the full admissible growth range. Our results extend the Schauder regularity theory for parabolic $p$-Laplace type equations to a broad class of possibly nonradial operators with Orlicz growth, while simplifying the regularity arguments and treating singular, degenerate, and mixed growth laws within a unified framework.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Alberto Antonini

item.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary fractional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system with different orders of dissipation. Our first result shows that every smooth solution satisfying the natural homogeneous Sobolev energy conditions is trivial whenever $1\leq\alpha\leq 5/3$ and $3\leq\alpha+2\beta\leq5$, without any additional integrability assumptions on the velocity or magnetic fields. This extends previous results to new parameter regimes, including cases with $\beta<1$. Beyond this region, we prove a complementary Liouville theorem under suitable integrability conditions only on the radial components of the velocity and magnetic fields. The proofs rely on the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and localized energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Albert Ai, Gaston Vergara-Hermosilla

item.title: Pointwise decay of steady Navier--Stokes flows with Navier-slip boundary condition in two-dimensional channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.27501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a pointwise decay estimate for steady incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in two-dimensional channels with positive Navier friction coefficient. Specifically, for the arbitrary-flux solutions constructed by Sha, Wang, and Xie \cite{SWX22f}, under suitable outlet conditions and weighted geometric bounds on the channel walls, we show \[ |\Bu(x_1,x_2)|\le \frac{C}{f(x_1)}, \] where $f$ is the channel width. Our decay rate is optimal in the cross-sectional supremum norm when the prescribed flux is nonzero. The main difficulty is that rescaling by the local width changes the Navier friction coefficient into a potentially large parameter. The key technique is to establish a local Stokes boundary estimate uniform in this parameter.
item.dc:creator: Han Li, Jingwen Han

item.title: Vanishing transport noise enhances stability of stratified Couette flow in the 3D Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2610.27650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the enhanced nonlinear stability of stably stratified Couette flow in the three-dimensional Boussinesq system driven by a common affine Stratonovich transport noise. Our main result shows that, for fixed $\beta>1/2$, suitably chosen noise amplitudes enlarge the range of perturbations for which we prove stability, even as they vanish with viscosity. For each fixed deterministic Sobolev perturbation satisfying the sufficient smallness conditions, the strong solution is global and obeys stability estimates on an event of prescribed high probability. No spatial localization or vanishing initial double means are required. The proof combines noise-induced mixing with coupled energy estimates to control nonlinear feedback and preserve the physical damping of the fast vertical velocity and temperature.
item.dc:creator: Lei Zhang

item.title: Spectral analysis of multi-bubble solutions to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.27752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate weighted spectral limits for separated multi-bubble configurations and refined spectral asymptotics for the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[ -\Delta u=u^p+\varepsilon u^q, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }\Omega, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Omega, \] where $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$ with $N\geq3$, $p=(N+2)/(N-2)$, $1\leq q<p$ and $\varepsilon$ is a positive parameter. We first determine the limits of the ordered weighted eigenvalues associated with families of positive functions admitting an $m$-bubble decomposition at distinct interior points with a remainder vanishing in $H_0^1(\Omega)$. The limiting eigenvalues are those of the single-bubble problem, with all multiplicities multiplied by $m$. We then refine this analysis for positive multi-bubble solutions of this problem with comparable concentration scales, deriving precise expansions of the first $(N+2)m$ eigenvalues and characterizing their eigenfunctions when $1<q<3$ if $N=4$ or $1\leq q<p$ if $N\geq5$. The leading corrections are determined by explicit symmetric matrices involving $q$, the concentration parameters, and the Green and Robin functions. In particular, we prove that the dilation matrix is positive definite. Together, these spectral results yield Morse index bounds for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, with an exact formula when the matrix governing the translation modes is invertible.
item.dc:creator: Minbo Yang, Shunneng Zhao

item.title: Orbital stability of standing waves for defocusing fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with a delta potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.27771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a delta potential and a repulsive nonlinearity in one space dimension is considered. First, it is proved that the Cauchy problem in Sobolev spaces on the real line is globally well-posed, independently of the sign of the delta potential. Moreover, in the case of an attractive delta potential, the existence, the minimization properties and the orbital stability of standing waves under the flow of the equation are established. The stability proof is based on concentration-compactness methods for the energy/charge functional. For that purpose, no explicit calculation of the standing waves is required and the results are based on the variational properties of the solutions alone.
item.dc:creator: Ram\'on G. Plaza, Miguel A. S\'anchez-Alc\'antara

item.title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.
item.dc:creator: Elena Danesi, Anne-Sophie de Suzzoni, Umberto Morellini

item.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $\mu$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Shaojie Yang, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Classification of positive solutions to the critical Lane-Emden system
item.description: arXiv:2610.27875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system $$ -\Delta u=v^p \, \, \text{in } \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, \, \, -\Delta v=u^q \, \, \text{in} \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $N\geq3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy $$ \frac{1}{p+1}+\frac{1}{q+1}=\frac{N-2}{N}.$$Without assuming boundedness, decay at infinity, or finite energy, we prove that every such solution has the form $$ u(x)=\lambda^{\frac{N}{q+1}}U(\lambda(x-a)), \, \, v(x)=\lambda^{\frac{N}{p+1}}V(\lambda(x-a)), $$ for some $a\in \mathbb{R}^N$ and $\lambda>0$, where $(U,V)$ is the positive radial ground state centered at the origin and normalized by $U(0)=1$. Consequently, both components are radially symmetric about the same point and satisfy $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}u^{q+1}\, dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}v^{p+1}\,dx<\infty. $$ Our result extends the classical classification of positive solutions of the critical Sobolev equation by Caffarelli, Gidas and Spruck and Chen and Li to the critical Lane-Emden system.
item.dc:creator: Yuxia Guo, Yichen Hu, Shaolong Peng, Tingfeng Yuan

item.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.27885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $\alpha > 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+\alpha^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-H\"ormander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $\alpha$, so that on the band $-\alpha^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Michiyuki Watanabe

item.title: The Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture for the Fisher-KPP equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture, which concerns the classification of all [0,1]-valued entire solutions of Fisher-KPP equations with concave C^2 reaction terms in arbitrary space dimension. We prove that every such solution is a C_{loc}^{1,2} limit of solutions generated by finitely many planar traveling fronts, possibly together with a spatially homogeneous solution. Our approach reveals an ordered linear structure underlying the nonlinear solution space, leading to a critical-subcritical spectral decomposition. The proof combines linear reconstruction of subcritical approximants with a measure representation (a kind of nonlinear Martin representation) of critical solutions, obtained through small-amplitude asymptotics and comparison with a radially symmetric entire solution.
item.dc:creator: Hongjun Guo, Kelei Wang, Maolin Zhou

item.title: Schr\"odinger estimates with arbitrarily small periodic regularity on $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{T}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.27920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M=\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{T}$ carry its product metric. We prove that the Schr\"odinger evolution maps $L^2(\mathbb{H}^2;H^s(\mathbb{T}))$ into $L^2([0,1];L^6(M))$ for every $s>0$, without any regularity assumption in the hyperbolic variable. The proof separates hyperbolic and periodic frequencies. A localized hyperbolic kernel estimate restricts the effective interaction time at hyperbolic frequency $L$ to order $L^{-1}$. Quadratic exponential sums then give a logarithmic bound when the periodic bandwidth is comparable to $L$. A mixed-norm decoupling argument, including an $L^6$-valued extension and a periodic transference step, reduces wider periodic bands to this case. The infimum of the admissible periodic regularities is therefore zero. The estimate at zero regularity is not established here.
item.dc:creator: Xuyi Wei

item.title: Kurzweil's impulsive inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.27950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present paper, we proceed with the research initiated in (S. Antontsev \emph{et al.}, Inverse Problems, 2021). We study the inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian and with a right-hand side in the integral over-determination condition, which approximates a discontinuous function at $t=0$. We rescale the problem in a neighbourhood $[0,1/n]$ and pass to the limit as $n$ approaches infinity. This leads to the inverse problem on an infinitesimal initial layer, which transforms the initial velocity into a new one.
item.dc:creator: Stanislav Antontsev, Pardeep Kumar, Ivan Kuznetsov

item.title: Stability of Serrin-Type Overdetermined Problems for the $p$-Laplacian and Related Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.27953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a Serrin-type overdetermined problem for the $p$-Laplacian and establish a quantitative stability estimate under suitable convexity and regularity assumptions on the domain, the solution, and the operator. Our method also applies to a class of generalized divergence-form elliptic operators.
item.dc:creator: Yingfang Zhang, Wenming Zou

item.title: A counterexample to the fractional Michael-Simon inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.27973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the fractional Michael-Simon inequality does not hold for general smooth hypersurfaces and for the range of 0 < s < (n-1)/n in the case p=1. We construct a family of smooth hypersurfaces, whose fractional mean curvature is nonnegative everywhere, which violates the inequality in the limit. The same construction yields a counterexample for every 1 \leq p < \infty for the range s < (n-1)/(np).
item.dc:creator: Vesa Julin, Giampiero Palatucci

item.title: Radial uniqueness and nondegeneracy for the Robin Lane-Emden equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study positive radial solutions of $-\Delta u=u^p$ in a ball $B_R\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, subject to the Robin boundary condition $\partial_\nu u+\beta u=0$, where $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$. For every Sobolev subcritical exponent $p>1$, we prove the existence of a unique positive radial solution and its nondegeneracy with respect to radial perturbations. The proof relies on the strict monotonicity of the logarithmic slope of the normalized Lane-Emden profile, which follows from the radial Pohozaev identity. When $N\ge3$, the same argument also recovers the classical critical existence range $0<\beta R<N-2$ and proves radial nondegeneracy throughout this interval. At $\beta R=(N-2)/2$, we exhibit $N$ linearly independent nonradial solutions of the linearized problem.
item.dc:creator: Jiaguo Li, Tianqi Xu

item.title: Mean-field limit and Vlasov equation for a Gaussian-thermostatted Lorentz gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.27992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study N particles moving in a dispersing billiard under an electric field and coupled through a Gaussian thermostat. The corresponding mean-field equation is a Vlasov-type equation with specular reflection. We reformulate the equation as a fixed point problem for the time-integrated thermostat coefficient. This yields existence of weak solutions for every absolutely continuous initial datum of finite energy and, for bounded initial densities supported on velocities that are large compared with the field, uniqueness of the weak solution; under the finite horizon assumption, the upper bound on the velocities can be replaced by an exponential tail of the initial density. In these regimes, we prove convergence of the empirical measures of the particle system to the solution of the kinetic equation. In general, convergence holds along subsequences.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Castorrini

item.title: A mean value formula for the p-Laplacian
item.description:
arXiv:2610.28022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce an asymptotic mean value formula of the form $u(x) - \B_\epsilon^p (u) (x) =\epsilon^2 \Delta_p u(x) + o(\epsilon^2)$ for the $p-$Laplacian, $\plap u := 
abla \cdot  ig( |
abla u |^{p-2} 
abla u  ig)$. Here $\B_\epsilon^p (u)$ is a nonlinear expression that involve the mean value and the surmemum/infimum of $u$ in suitable balls. This asymptotic mean value formula allows us to characterize viscosity solutions to equations with different homogeneities in different sets of variables, like $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=f(x)$ (for $x=(x',x'') \in\mathbb{R}^d$, $x'=(x_1,...,x_n)$ and $x''=(x_{n+1,...,x_d})$), and the parabolic $p$-Laplace heat equation $\partial_t u (x,t)-\Delta_p u(x,t)=0$. Moreover, the resulting asymptotic mean value formulas are related to two-player zero sum games whose value functions, characterized as the unique solution to the corresponding dynamic programming principle, converge as the parameter that controls the size of the steps in the game goes to zero, to the unique viscosity solution to the corresponding boundary value problem for the operator under consideration. Finally, we also include a Holder regularity result for $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=0$ proved using the game theoretical interpretation of the problem.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Fuertes-Moran, Julio D. Rossi

item.title: A Quantitative Robin Faber-Krahn Inequality in Terms of Eigenfunction Distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.28032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian with positive Robin boundary conditions. For every open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ of prescribed volume, we prove that \[ \lambda_{1,\beta}(\Omega)-\lambda_{1,\beta}(B) \geq c\|u_\Omega-u_B\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}^4, \] where $B$ is a ball achieving the Fraenkel asymmetry of $\Omega$, and $u_\Omega$ and $u_B$ are nonnegative, $L^2$-normalized first Robin eigenfunctions, extended by zero outside their respective domains. The constant $c>0$ depends only on the dimension, the Robin parameter, and the prescribed volume. The exponent $4$ is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Nitsch, Cristina Trombetti, Federico Villone

item.title: Schauder estimates for ratios of elliptic solutions under zero set inclusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.28077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $u,v$ be two nontrivial functions that solve $$ \mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla v)=0\qquad\mathrm{in \ }B_r\subset\mathbb R^n,\quad n\geq2,\quad r>0, $$ with $A$ symmetric, uniformly elliptic and Lipschitz continuous, and assume the zero set inclusion $Z(u)\subseteq Z(v)$. We prove that the ratio $w=v/u$ continuously extends, together with its gradient, across $Z(u)=\{u=0\}$. In particular, $w\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_{r})$ for any $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Furthermore, given any integer $k\geq2$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, if $A\in C^{k-1,\alpha}(B_r)$, then $w\in C^{k,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_{r})$. The estimates are uniform in classes of coefficients $A$ with prescribed ellipticity and regularity bounds, and in normalized classes of denominators $u$ with uniformly bounded doubling constant.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Vita

item.title: On the Allen--Cahn equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that finite Morse index implies $O(R^{n-1})$ energy growth for bounded entire solutions of the quartic Allen--Cahn equation in dimensions $4\leq n\leq9$, uniformly in the center of the ball. Combined with the cited finite-index classification results, this gives planar rigidity for $4\leq n\leq7$ and, for nonconstant solutions, multiplicity-one stable minimal cone blowdowns through dimension nine. The proof uses an additive interaction estimate for adjacent transition layers, a weighted curvature and defect estimate with exponent $p=9/4$, and a common test function for penalized reach and ambient stability. The local interaction coefficient $48$ is optimal in the class specified by the low-defect hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Space-time localized nonuniqueness for the inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove space-time localized nonuniqueness for the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus. For every $0<s<3/2$ and $p>1$ sufficiently close to one, we construct weak solutions with strictly positive density in $C_tL^p$ and velocity in $C_tH^s$. These solutions approximate prescribed smooth density and velocity fields satisfying the necessary mass and spatial first moment conditions, while agreeing with a given smooth solution outside a compact subset of a prescribed cylinder. In particular, there are infinitely many nontrivial solutions which coincide with the rest state outside that cylinder and whose density is not renormalized. The proof uses convex integration with concentrated density profiles transported exactly by the perturbed velocity. Nonnegative coefficients cancel the continuity defect and the stress simultaneously. A stationary density corrector preserves positivity through successive corrections, and compactly supported inverse divergence operators preserve spatial localization.
item.dc:creator: Xingyu Li

item.title: Navier-Stokes flow past a translating body: attainability of the steady state as limit of an $L^p$ weak solution
item.description: arXiv:2610.28150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a viscous, incompressible, Newtonian fluid that fills the region of space exterior to a rigid body. Let the fluid be activated by a perturbation $u_0\in L^p(\OO)$, $p\in (2,3)$ and let the body start to translate with a prescribed velocity $-h(t)u_\infty$, $t>0$, $u_\infty\in\R^3\setminus \{0\}$. Suppose that the body reaches the stationary regime after some finite time. We show that, under suitable assumptions on $u_\infty$, a steady state is always reachable by the fluid, asymptotically in time, as limit of a suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes flow in suitable metrics. Our result seems to be a further contribution related to the {\it Starting Problem}, posed by R. Finn in 1965.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Palma

item.title: The Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish geometric and analytic rigidity results for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation. On a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the existence of a positive critical point of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg quotient forces the manifold to be Euclidean and the solution to be extremal. No minimizing assumption or volume growth hypothesis is required, thereby strengthening earlier rigidity results. In Euclidean space, we prove that all positive solutions of the normalized equation whose nonlinear mass on expanding annuli has sublinear growth are extremals. The linear threshold is optimal, as shown by explicit profiles that are constant in one direction. We also prove a sharp pointwise estimate involving the solution and its gradient, valid without assumptions at infinity, with equality at one point characterizing the extremals. The proofs use weighted divergence identities and a reflection argument controlled by annular mass. Explicit constructions reveal the geometric and variational limits of rigidity: nonflat quotient critical points exist beyond the curvature hypothesis, while the normalized equation admits positive solutions even under strictly positive sectional curvature and maximal volume growth.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Catino, Dario Daniele Monticelli, Alberto Roncoroni

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of the singular set in optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.28228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal transport between bounded smooth domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with smooth positive densities bounded above and below. Without convexity assumptions on the domains, we prove that the optimal map is smooth outside a relatively closed set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-1$.
item.dc:creator: Shibing Chen, Qi-Rui Li, Yuanyuan Li, Jiakun Liu, Xiaotian Wu

item.title: Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.28230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8\pi$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates do not rule out growth as time tends to infinity, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Hosono

item.title: Small Viscosity Limit of Navier-Stokes Equations in A Quarter Plane with Navier Slip Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the vanishing-viscosity limit of Leray solutions to the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a quarter plane with Navier slip boundary conditions on both edges for a class of compatible well-prepared initial data. By multi-scale analysis, we deduce that a boundary layer of order $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ arises near each edge of the corner and is described by a linearized Prandtl equation, and near the corner, their overlap and nonlinear interaction are captured by a two-dimensional corner profile. Although this profile occurs at order $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$, it is governed, in the fast variables, by a nonlinear initial-boundary value problem of Navier--Stokes type. The well-posedness and Sobolev regularity of the outer flow problems, together with the well-posedness and weighted estimates of the boundary-layer and corner-layer problems are obtained on a common time interval $[0,T]$ independent of $\epsilon$. To ensure the required regularity of the outer Euler flow in the critical right-angle domain, it is assumed that the initial vorticity of the outer leading order flow vanishes in a neighborhood of the corner. We then rigorously justify the resulting composite expansion in the small viscosity limit. More precisely, after retaining the leading outer flow, the two weak boundary layers, the nonlinear corner layer, and the order-$\epsilon$ outer correction, the error between the exact solution and this truncated expansion is $O(\epsilon^{5/4})$ in $L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\Q))$ and $O(\epsilon^{3/4})$ in $L^2(0,T;H^1(\Q))$.
item.dc:creator: Wen Guo, Ya-Guang Wang

item.title: Nonlocal geometric rigidity inequalities and the justification of linearized peridynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.28268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove geometric rigidity inequalities for vector fields using double-integral Gagliardo-type quantities. We show that the nonlocal-norm distance of the difference quotient of a vector field from the difference quotient of a single rigid motion is controlled by the same nonlocal norm of a difference characterizing the distance to the manifold of all rigid motions. The inequality is then used to show the variational convergence of a sequence of rescaled nonlocal fully nonconvex integral functionals to a linearized energy functional. Related functionals arise in peridynamic formulations of continuum mechanics via the total strain energy; this variational convergence provides a rigorous justification of linearized peridynamics with volume constraint via the convergence of rescaled displacements. We additionally establish analogous rigidity inequalities in the linearized setting, which can be thought of as nonlocal analogues of Korn's inequality for displacements.
item.dc:creator: James M. Scott

item.title: Stability of 2D MHD with Only Horizontal Dissipation near a Background Magnetic Field on $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description:
arXiv:2610.28308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with dissipation in only one direction are stable in $H^2$ on the whole plane is a well-known open problem: without transverse dissipation, a cubic interaction fails to be time-integrable. We show that a magnetic field removes this obstruction. For the 2D incompressible MHD equations on $\mathbb R^2$ in which both the viscosity $
u$ and the magnetic diffusivity $\mu$ act only in the horizontal direction, we prove the global nonlinear $H^2$ stability of every background field $\gamma e_2$ aligned with the non-dissipative direction, with a stability threshold that is explicit in $
u$, $\mu$ and $\gamma$. The stabilizing mechanism is genuinely nonlinear: at the linear level the background field produces no damping at all in the vertical direction. Instead, in Els"asser variables the obstruction becomes an interaction between Alfv'en waves travelling in opposite directions, and we identify nonlinear dissipative quantities that measure the overlap of these waves and are time-integrable although neither wave decays. We then sharpen the threshold by a space--time div--curl estimate for balance laws in the $(t,x_2)$-plane. For $
u=\mu\leq1\leq\gamma$, the admissible perturbations are of size $
u^{2/3}\gamma^{1/3}$, improving the direct scale $
u$ and growing without bound as the background field strengthens.
item.dc:creator: Jiahong Wu, Mengxin Yan, Ning Zhu, Yi Zhu

item.title: Optimal power concavity of the variational mean curvature via singular $1$-Laplace problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded convex domain and let $H_{\Omega}\leq 0$ denote its variational mean curvature, in the sense of Barozzi, Gonzalez and Tamanini [PAMS, 1987]. We prove that $-H_{\Omega}$ is harmonic convex, that is $1/H_{\Omega}$ is a convex function in $\Omega$, and that the exponent $-1$ is optimal in the class of convex domains. This strictly improves the concavity of $H_{\Omega}$ obtained by Alter and Caselles [Nonlinear Anal., 2009], who also proved, by geometric methods, a closely related property for the classical mean curvature under Minkowski interpolation of convex bodies. Our approach is analytic: the result is deduced from a concavity property of the solution of the singular $1$-Laplace Dirichlet problem $$\begin{cases} -\Delta_1 u = {u^{-\gamma}} & \quad \hbox{in $\Omega$}, \\ u = 0 &\quad \hbox{on $\partial \Omega$}, \end{cases}$$ for $\gamma \in (0,1]$, whose unique positive solution is $u=(-H_{\Omega})^{-1/\gamma}$. We show that $u^{\gamma}$ is concave, and we obtain this by proving that the solutions $u_p$ of the approximating problems $-\Delta_p u_p = u_p^{-\gamma}$ are $\frac{p-1+\gamma}{p}$-concave on every bounded convex domain, without any boundary regularity, and then letting $p\to 1^+$. Explicit examples show that no H\"older continuity of $H_{\Omega}$ up to $\partial\Omega$ holds uniformly in the class of convex domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary.
item.dc:creator: Marco Gallo, Francesco Petitta, Marco Squassina

item.title: Thin-Layer Dichotomy in Three-Phase Mullins-Sekerka Flow: Gap Dynamics and Composite Interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the thin-layer limit of the Mullins-Sekerka flow in concentric circular geometries at fixed wave number $k$, contrasting a two-phase annulus with a genuine three-phase layer. A dichotomy emerges: for $k\ge2$ the rates blow up like the inverse thickness when the same phase lies on both sides of the layer, whereas between two different phases the matrix governing the linearized Fourier mode extends analytically to zero thickness. Both cases share the singular Dirichlet-to-Neumann factor of the thin annulus and differ only in whether the Gibbs-Thomson law forces an order-one potential difference across it. In the three-phase case the pure thickness-modulation rate stays below the logarithmic growth rate of the mean thickness, for every $k\ge1$ and all positive tensions, and, after projection onto the mean displacement and the outer interface, the collapsed pair moves as one interface carrying the sum of the two tensions. All statements concern the instantaneous fixed-mode linearization. The singularity is a property of the phase coupling, not of the thin geometry.
item.dc:creator: Tokuhiro Eto

item.title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge--Amp\`ere Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an interior $C^2$ estimate for locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solutions of the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$ under weak quadratic growth bounds on sufficiently large balls, where $f$ is positive and Dini-continuous. We assume a distributional lower bound for the Laplacian of $f^{1/n}$. The main ingredient is a pseudo-$C^2$ estimate using the Green-function averaging error, valid also when $f$ is nonnegative. As an application, we prove that every entire Bedford-Taylor solution of $\det(u_{i\bar j})=1$ with weak quadratic growth is a real quadratic polynomial, resolving a conjecture of G\'abor Sz\'ekelyhidi.
item.dc:creator: Jingchen Hu, Li Sheng

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. Building on \cite{Collot2023}, which constructed 2D horizontally odd solutions where the on-axis derivative $\partial_X u(t,0,Z)$ blows up at rate $(T-t)^{-1}$ with boundary concentration scale $|\ln (T-t)|^{-1}$, this paper characterizes this blow-up as forming between hyperbolic stagnation points. We derive precise asymptotic expansions for on-axis derivatives beyond leading order, identifying a horizontal concentration scale of $(T-t)^{3/2}$ characteristic of generic Burgers' singularities. Furthermore, we justify the 2D solution's expansion near the symmetry axis by proving $(T-t)^{3/2}$ is a universal lower bound on the radius of analyticity.
item.dc:creator: Charles Collot, Slim Ibrahim, Lingjun Qian

item.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for p-capacity of compact sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.28421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the capacitary Brunn-Minkowski inequality for arbitrary nonempty compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, and every $1<p<\infty$, with no assumption of convexity, connectedness, interior, or boundary regularity. For $1<p<n$ the inequality is for the variational $p$-capacity. For $p>n$ it is for the capacity determined by the constant term at infinity of the normalized $p$-harmonic Green's function with pole at infinity, and for $p=n$ for an outer regularization of this quantity, which agrees with it for $n$-regular sets and in the plane is a constant multiple of logarithmic capacity. In particular, it holds for Newtonian capacity of all compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$, and for logarithmic capacity of all planar compact sets. Previously these inequalities were known for convex sets and, for logarithmic capacity, for planar continua. When both capacities are positive, equality holds for $0<\lambda<1$ if and only if the filled sets, obtained by adjoining the bounded components of the complement, are convex and equal up to translation and dilation. This characterization is new for nonconvex sets, even for Newtonian and logarithmic capacity.
item.dc:creator: Murat Akman

item.title: Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $\Psi$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.28463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $\mu\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $\Psi$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $\Psi$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.
item.dc:creator: Nelson R. Ojeda, Ruben D. Spies

item.title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
item.description: arXiv:2610.28481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-\Delta u=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-\Delta u=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.
item.dc:creator: Xue Li

item.title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.28503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zhou, Yingfang Zhang, Wenming Zou

item.title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(\Delta_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Castellanos

item.title: Local crystallization in three-dimensional quantization
item.description: arXiv:2610.28547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A long-standing conjecture on the quantization problem due to Gersho, which remains open in dimensions higher than two, posits that optimal quantizers crystallize into a lattice structure; in dimension three, the natural candidate is the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, known to be optimal among other lattices. In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.
item.dc:creator: Ata Deniz Aydin, Mikaela Iacobelli

item.title: Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.28549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two conceptually different local well-posedness results for wave kinetic equations associated with water-wave systems. For pure gravity waves with 2D interfaces, we establish a classical well-posedness theory in weighted Sobolev spaces: regularity is propagated, and solutions depend continuously on the initial data in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with one-dimensional interfaces, the situation is fundamentally different. We prove well-posedness in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces (in the sense of existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology), but we also show that, in general, any additional regularity of the initial data is instantly lost. Moreover, continuity in time and continuous dependence on the initial data fail in the weighted $L^\infty$ norm, even for smooth compactly supported initial data. This instability is caused by degenerate three-wave resonances, which produce singular collision rates and arbitrarily short relaxation time scales. The distinction between the two theories reflects a fundamental difference in their resonant geometry.
item.dc:creator: Yu Deng, Alexandru D. Ionescu, Fabio Pusateri

item.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Castellanos

item.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.
item.dc:creator: Vitalii Shpakivskyi

item.title: Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure
item.dc:creator: {\L}ukasz P{\l}ociniczak, Hubert Woszczek

item.title: Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Pablo Tejerina-P\'erez, Leonid Sarieddine, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez, Marisol Traforetti, Pau Sol\'e-Vilar\'o, Oleksii Ignatenko, Nazar Tkach, Pavlos Protopapas

item.title: $L^{p}$-parabolicity of Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are H\"older conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1<p\leq 2$ as well as a sharp volume condition for all $1<p<\infty$ for manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature and for model manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Grigor'yan, Leandro F. Pessoa, Alberto G. Setti

item.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.27343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Cristian Gonz\'alez-Riquelme, Claudio Mu\~noz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas

item.title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.27500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-\gamma Q^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, \gamma >0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.
item.dc:creator: Chandler Haight, Alex D Rodriguez, Svetlana Roudenko

item.title: Global Mizohata-Takeuchi for Indicator Weights of Bounded Complexity in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.27659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the global Mizohata-Takeuchi estimate for bounded complexity weights in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and an arbitrary $C^2$ uniformly convex curve on the Fourier side, with an implied constant depending only on the complexity and the curve. A version with a logarithmic loss follows from a short argument using the $T^*T$ method and the main estimate of Basu, Guo, Zhang, and Zorin-Kranich (2026). The main effort of this paper is devoted to removing the logarithmic factor. To achieve this, we use tools from semialgebraic geometry and adapt and develop ideas of Ricci and Stein (1987). As a by-product, we obtain a uniform geometric inequality for planar regions of bounded complexity that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Hao, Ruyi Wang, Ruixiang Zhang

item.title: P\'olya's conjecture for Dirichlet eigenvalues of spherical shells and Aharonov--Bohm annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.27707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish strict Dirichlet P\'olya inequalities for spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$ and for every radius ratio. The inclusive eigenvalue counting function lies strictly below the leading Weyl term at every positive energy; consequently, each eigenvalue strictly exceeds its Weyl prediction, with multiplicities included. We also prove the same strict inequality for the Aharonov--Bohm operator on planar annuli at arbitrary flux. In dimension two, the nonmagnetic result gives a fully analytic proof of the planar annulus theorem of Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sher (J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2026). The common ingredient is a lattice-point bound for the shell action, uniform in the starting point of a tail and in the lattice translation. Quadrature for the inverse action controls the change of convexity caused by the inner boundary. The tail estimate supplies the hypothesis of the known dimension-reduction argument for balls, while lattice translations represent the magnetic flux. Laptev's product argument yields corresponding strict bounds on products of shells and nonempty bounded open sets.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: The Great Picard theorem for quasiregular values
item.description: arXiv:2610.27976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a version of Rickman's Great Picard theorem in the theory of quasiregular values. The version of the theorem that we prove is in fact stated in terms of omitted quasiregular values, unlike the previously known Little Picard theorem of the theory that is based on quasiregular values in the boundary of the image set. As a byproduct of the proof, we also prove a Riemann removability theorem in our setting, which ends up strengthening the conclusion of the previously resolved question of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin.
item.dc:creator: Ilmari Kangasniemi, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.28026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez

item.title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.28037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving theorems of Bourgain and Badger--Genschaw, we prove that the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure on any domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\mathbb{R}^4$, and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq3$ is at most $3-10^{-5}$, $4-10^{-7}$, and $n-(n-1)^{-(2n+6.12\sqrt{n})}$, respectively. The previous bounds in dimensions $3$ and $4$ were $3-10^{-15}$ and $4-10^{-26}$, while Bishop conjectures that the sharp bound is $n-(n-1)^{-1}$. The main difficulty in optimizing Bourgain's method is estimating non-additive $s$-dimensional Hausdorff-type contents when $s<n$ is close to $n$. Previous arguments used net contents associated to a fixed $m$-adic lattice, with $m$ large depending on $n$. We redevelop the dimension theory using pairwise disjoint cubes in general position and obtain a new estimate showing that one thin ring without large holes surrounding a cube makes it unlikely for Brownian motion to reach the cube before exiting the domain. A key feature of the construction is that the holes are round rather than rectangular. We also propose ten challenges on the dimension of harmonic measure that may provide accessible targets en route to Bishop's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Michael Albert, Matthew Badger, Alyssa Genschaw

item.title: On the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on forms of the unit Euclidean ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.28181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on differential $p$-forms over the unit Euclidean ball. We apply it to test how far one of Kuttler-Sigillito inequalities is from being optimal.
item.dc:creator: Rodolphe Abou Assali

item.title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation II
item.description: arXiv:2610.28606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxiang Wang, Wenlong Wang

item.title: A quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a large class of unbounded potentials
item.description: arXiv:2410.01346v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a quantitative Borg-Levinson theorem for a broad class of unbounded potentials when the spatial dimension is five or greater. In the final section, we outline the modifications required to extend the main result to the anisotropic case.
item.dc:creator: Mourad Choulli

item.title: On the dispersive estimates for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation on a honeycomb lattice
item.description: arXiv:2503.08996v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The discrete Schr\"odinger equation on a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice is a fundamental tight-binding approximation model that describes the propagation of waves on graphene. For free evolution, we first show that the degenerate frequencies of the dispersion relation are completely characterized by three symmetric periodic curves (Theorem 2.1), and that the three curves meet at Dirac points where conical singularities appear (see Figure 2.1). Based on this observation, we prove the $L^1\to L^\infty$ dispersion estimates for the linear flow depending on the frequency localization (Theorem 2.3). Collecting all, we obtain the dispersion estimate with $O(|t|^{-2/3})$ decay as well as Strichartz estimates. As an application, we prove small data scattering for a nonlinear model (Theorem 2.10). The proof of the key dispersion estimates is based on the associated oscillatory integral estimates with degenerate phases and conical singularities at Dirac points. Our proof is direct and uses only elementary methods.
item.dc:creator: Younghun Hong, Yukihide Tadano, Changhun Yang

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to critical Hartree equations with isolated singularities
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Henrique Andrade, Tao Feng, Paolo Piccione, Minbo Yang

item.title: Upper bound on heat kernels of finite particle systems of Keller-Segel type
item.description: arXiv:2508.10892v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain an upper bound on the heat kernel of the finite particle approximation of the Keller-Segel model of chemotaxis. The proof exploits a connection with certain non-local operators. We also obtain upper heat kernel bounds for related systems of interacting Brownian and stable particles that exhibit similar local blow-up effects.
item.dc:creator: S. E. Boutiah, D. Kinzebulatov

item.title: Mixed local-nonlocal equations with critical nonlinearity on $\mathbb{R}^N$: Non-existence, Existence, and Multiplicity of positive solutions
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis (2026)
item.dc:creator: Nirjan Biswas, Souptik Chakraborty, Paramananda Das

item.title: A deterministic particle approximation for a fourth-order equation
item.description: arXiv:2512.11441v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a deterministic particle approximation to a fourth order equation with applications in cell-cell adhesion. In order to do that, first we show that the equation can be asymptotically obtained as a limit from a class of well-posed nonlocal partial differential equations. These latter have the advantage that the particles' empirical measure naturally satisfies the equation. Afterwards, we obtain stability of the 2-Wasserstein gradient flow of this family of nonlocal equations that we use in order to recover a deterministic particle approximation of the fourth order equation. Up to our knowledge, in this manuscript we derive the first deterministic particle approximation for a fourth-order partial differential equation. Finally, we give some numerical simulations of the model at the particles level.
item.dc:creator: Charles Elbar, Alejandro Fern\'andez-Jim\'enez

item.title: $\Gamma$-convergence of free discontinuity problems for circle-valued maps in the linear regime
item.description: arXiv:2601.20612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the $\Gamma$-convergence of Ambrosio-Tortorelli type-functionals for circle valued functions, in the case of volume terms with linear growth. We show the emergence of a non-local $\Gamma$-limit, which is due to the topological structure of the target space, and discuss compactness of minimal liftings. Our results extend the analysis of a previous work on the quadratic case. Applications to the area functional are given.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Bellettini, Roberta Marziani, Riccardo Scala

item.title: Quantitative Landis-type result for Dirac operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.16049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantitative unique continuation at infinity for Dirac equations with bounded matrix-valued potentials. For the massless Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we establish a Landis-type estimate showing that the vanishing order of any nontrivial bounded solution of $( \mathcal{D}_n + \mathbb{V} ) \varphi = 0$ satisfies a lower bound of order $\exp(-\kappa R^{2} (\log R)^{2})$ as $|x|=R\to \infty$; the quadratic growth in the exponent is sharp, in view of previous known results. Our proof follows a Bourgain--Kenig type approach based on a Carleman inequality for Dirac operators which relies on a local H\"older regularity result, which we also prove. In two dimension, we obtain improved quantitative estimates under symmetry assumptions on the potential $\mathbb{V}$ and for real-valued solutions. Finally, we also derive qualitative Landis-type results for Dirac equations with decaying potentials, including critical decay rates.
item.dc:creator: Ujjal Das, Luca Fanelli, Luz Roncal

item.title: Quantitative unique continuation for elliptic equations with H\"older continuous potentials
item.description: arXiv:2603.21392v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantitative unique continuation for second order elliptic equations with lower-order terms of H\"older regularity via a weighted frequency function method. We establish quantitative three-ball inequalities and corresponding vanishing-order bounds for Schr\"odinger equations with H\"older potentials and H\"older gradient terms, and corresponding results for elliptic equations with variable leading coefficients. Our results are quantitative with explicit dependence of H\"older norms in the three-ball inequalities. These fill in the gap for quantitative unique continuation between bounded potentials and $C^1$ potentials.
item.dc:creator: Long Teng, Zhiwei Wang, Jiuyi Zhu

item.title: Widely degenerate anisotropic diffusion: local boundedness and semicontinuity
item.description: arXiv:2604.20597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the regularity of local weak solutions to evolution equations of the form \[ \partial_{t}u\,=\,\sum_{i=1}^{n}\,\partial_{x_{i}}\left[a_{i}(x,t)\,(\vert\partial_{x_{i}}u\vert-\delta_{i})_{+}^{p_{i}-1}\,\frac{\partial_{x_{i}}u}{\vert\partial_{x_{i}}u\vert}\right]\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\mathrm{in}\,\,\,\Omega_{T}\,=\,\Omega\times(0,T)\,, \] where $\Omega$ is a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $n\geq2$, the coefficients $a_{i}$ are measurable and bounded, $p_{i}>1$ and $\delta_{i}\geq0$ are fixed parameters. Under suitable assumptions on the exponents $p_{i}$, we first show that the local boundedness of weak solutions follows from their membership in an appropriate non-homogeneous parabolic De Giorgi class. We then establish the existence of semicontinuous representatives for local weak sub(super)-solutions. Our analysis extends analogous results available for less degenerate operators and generalizes the local boundedness results obtained in [7] to fully anisotropic, widely degenerate parabolic PDEs with non-smooth coefficients depending additionally on the space-time variables $(x,t)$, whose growth is governed by a family of exponents $p_{i}$ rather than by a single exponent.
item.dc:creator: Pasquale Ambrosio, Simone Ciani, Giovanni Cupini

item.title: Well-posedness and Stability of Thermoelastic Suspension Bridges with Cattaneo Heat Conduction: The Role of Viscoelastic Memory
item.description: arXiv:2606.12786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermoelastic suspension bridges operate under strong thermo-mechanical coupling, and the classical Fourier law fails to capture the finite speed of thermal propagation observed in low-conductivity materials such as concrete. This paper investigates a suspension bridge model in which the heat flux is governed by the Cattaneo law with relaxation time $\tau$, and in which the bridge deck may or may not possess viscoelastic memory. Using operator semigroup theory, we establish well-posedness and derive sharp decay rates for both regimes. For the memoryless system ($\delta=0$), we show that the semigroup is polynomially stable with rate $t^{-1/2}$ when the structural parameters satisfy $\frac{\rho_1}{\kappa} = \frac{\rho_2}{b}$, and that the rate deteriorates to $t^{-1/4}$ otherwise; moreover, exponential stability fails whenever $\chi_0 \neq 0$, or $\chi_0 = 0$ and $\chi_1 = 0$, where $\chi_0$ and $\chi_1$ are parameter-dependent coefficients. In sharp contrast, when viscoelastic memory is present ($\delta=1$), the semigroup becomes exponentially stable, regardless of the structural parameter ratio. This reveals a regularizing role of viscoelastic memory: it converts polynomial decay into exponential decay and removes the parameter-ratio obstruction. The results provide a theoretical basis for exploiting inherent viscoelasticity in long-span bridges and for optimizing deck parameters in memoryless structures.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhou, Jiamin He

item.title: Sharp Riesz and reverse Riesz inequalities for degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type
item.description: arXiv:2607.15599v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the sharp $L^p$ ranges of the Riesz transform and the reverse Riesz inequality for a class of power-degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type. When the degenerate variable has dimension at least two, the Riesz transform is bounded throughout the reflexive range. In dimension one, a capacity-driven transition occurs: weak degeneracy produces a sharp finite upper endpoint, whereas strong degeneracy separates the two half-lines and restores the full range. The reverse inequality displays a different sharp phenomenon. In the weakly degenerate one-dimensional regime it holds throughout the reflexive range except at a single Hardy-critical exponent, while in all remaining regimes it holds for every $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Dangyang He

item.title: Self-Similar Solutions of the Two-Dimensional Incompressible Euler Equation from Large Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2607.19700v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $0<a<1$ and any $C^1$, divergence-free, $(-a)$-homogeneous vector field $u_0$ on the punctured plane, we construct a forward self-similar solution of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on the plane with initial datum $u_0$. No smallness or sign condition is required. The solution is obtained as a vanishing-dissipation limit of hypodissipative self-similar profiles. The key estimate is a uniform vorticity profile bound in the critical Lorentz space $L^{\frac{2}{1+a},\infty}$. The resulting velocity has locally finite energy and converges strongly to $u_0$ locally in $L^2$ as time approaches zero.
