The vorticity preserves its distribution function and converges strongly to the initial vorticity locally in $L^{\frac{2}{1+a}-}$ as time approaches zero.
item.dc:creator: Hyungjun Choi

item.title: The Follow-the-Leader scheme with non-monotone velocity
item.description: arXiv:2607.28195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the approximation of entropy solutions to a one-dimensional scalar conservation law via the so-called Follow-the-Leader particle scheme in case the velocity map is \emph{non monotone}. The result is based on a discrete maximum principle, on $BV$ estimates of the approximated density, and on the characterization of the limit as entropy solution in the sense of Kru\v zkov.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Francesco

item.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2608.05077v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a \emph{point-free} theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and solve a generalized Sylvester equation that controls the commutator between the differential structure and the highly oscillatory material properties. This abstract perspective unifies stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media--and their respective convergence rates--are entirely captured by the behavior of the spectral measures of the microscopic and macroscopic derivative operators near zero frequency.
item.dc:creator: Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jim\'enez Bola\~nos

item.title: Positive solutions for an indefinite-weight Minkowski mean curvature Neumann problem: multiplicity and asymptotic behaviour
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Ziegele

item.title: Vanishing boundary geometry and critical pressure compactness for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.13223v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove boundary partial regularity for the three-dimensional nonstationary Navier--Stokes equations in bounded domains with fractional Sobolev boundary graphs whose integrability exponent is greater than three. Within the fractional Sobolev graph setting, this lowers the boundary threshold from fifteen quarters to three. We work in Breit's boundary suitable weak-solution framework, with the mixed maximal-regularity pair $(5/3,15/14)$ explicitly included in the solution assumptions. The main difficulty is to recover pressure compactness without imposing higher regularity on the rough boundary coefficients. After a rigid rotation to the tangent plane and parabolic rescaling, we show that each boundary graph becomes small in both Sobolev multiplier classes needed for the local energy inequality and the critical Stokes estimate. Geometry and fluid excess enter a contradiction argument as independent small parameters, so the limiting problem is the standard flat Stokes system. A localized pressure decomposition separates the vanishing nonlinear and coefficient errors from the forced and homogeneous flat pressures. The error pressure converges strongly at the critical mixed integrability pair, whereas higher spatial integrability is used only for the flat problems. These estimates yield a one-step excess decay bound with a constant independent of the contraction radius. A physical-scale iteration, followed by interior--boundary Campanato patching, gives local parabolic H\"older continuity of the velocity at every regular boundary point when the force has integrability exponent greater than five halves. The boundary singular set is relatively closed and has zero parabolic Hausdorff measure in dimension five thirds. The geometric decay determines a uniform starting scale and does not restrict the final regularity exponent.
item.dc:creator: Leyang Wang

item.title: Global Sobolev Convergence of Howard Iteration for Finite-Horizon Controlled Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2609.15607v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Howard policy iteration for finite-horizon stochastic control problems in which the control enters the diffusion coefficient. Each iteration selects a policy by maximizing the Hamiltonian and evaluates it through a linear parabolic equation. Since the improvement depends on the Hessian, even smooth data can produce discontinuous evaluation coefficients. We prove global convergence in the full parabolic Sobolev space under assumptions that allow this loss of regularity. In one space dimension, bounded measurable coefficients and uniform ellipticity suffice, without a large discount, a short horizon, small diffusion variation, or regularity assumptions on the improving policies. Multidimensional extensions hold under structural conditions on the diffusion matrix. The proof combines monotonicity with a parabolic growth estimate to show that the Bellman residual vanishes in measure. Uniform higher integrability then yields strong convergence of the values, gradients, Hessians, and time derivatives, and constructs the unique strong solution. We also establish residual error bounds, extend the argument to entropy regularization and zero-temperature limits, and obtain quadratic convergence for special one-dimensional models.
item.dc:creator: Linyu Miao

item.title: Continuous sonic-supersonic flows in two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzles
item.description: arXiv:2609.23415v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper concerns continuous sonic-supersonic flows in a two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzle with straight solid walls. For a given inlet that is a small perturbation of an arc centered at the vertex of the nozzle, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of a continuous sonic-supersonic potential flow which is close to the radially symmetric sonic-supersonic flow. The flow is sonic at the inlet, with its velocity along the normal direction, and becomes supersonic in the nozzle. Such a sonic-supersonic model is governed by a quasilinear nonstrictly hyperbolic equation with degeneracy at the inlet, and the degeneracy is weak in the sense that there exist exactly two distinct characteristics from each sonic point, except for those at the walls, pointing into the supersonic region. One of the crucial ingredients of the analysis is to obtain the precise asymptotic behavior near the sonic inlet by the method of characteristics, which is essential for establishing the local existence of continuous sonic-supersonic flows. Another one is to extend the local solution globally and derive uniform estimates in the supersonic region.
item.dc:creator: Lili Qian, Chunpeng Wang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Light rays of Lorentzian graphs and the Born-Infeld model
item.description: arXiv:2609.25449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Following a program outlined by Bartnik, and also employing nonlinear potential techniques we developed in the last years, we study lightlike singularities of variational solutions to the prescribed Lorentzian mean curvature equation with possibly unbounded (rough) curvature. This corresponds to allowing for unbounded charges in the Born-Infeld model.
item.dc:creator: Cristiana De Filippis, Giuseppe Mingione

item.title: A minimization problem for a cooperative system with a degenerate Bernoulli weight
item.description: arXiv:2609.25544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study local minimizers of the energy functional$J(\mathbf{u}) = \int_D (|\nabla \mathbf{u}|^2 + Q^2(x)\chi_{\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}})\,dx$ which give rise to a singular cooperative system. Here \(\mathbf{u}=(u_1,\dots,u_m): D\to\R_+^m\) is a vector-valued unknown function, \(\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}:=\{|\mathbf{u}|>0\}\) is the positive set, \(\chi_{\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}}\) is the characteristic function of the positive set \(\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\), and \(Q(x)\) is the Bernoulli weight function. This problem was first introduced by Caffarelli, Shahgholian, and Yeressian in the poineer work ({\it Duke Math. J.} \textbf{167}(10), 2018), where the regularity theory for minimizers and for the free boundary \(\partial\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\) was established for nondegenerate Bernoulli weights, i.e., \(Q(x)\ge Q_{\rm min}>0\). The present paper studies the same free boundary problem but for a degenerate Bernoulli weight. The main difficulty lies in the coupling between the degeneracy of \(Q(x)\) and the vector-valued nature of the problem. We show that the the free boundary set \(\partial\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\cap\{Q(x)=0\}\) decomposes into a nondegenerate part and a degenerate part. Nondegenerate points admit nontrivial blow-up limits; degenerate points have zero weighted density. We classify nondegenerate points into single-phase, multi-phase non-branching, and multi-phase branching points, analyzing their geometric structure. The branching-point singular structure for multi-phase points is purely vectorial and new in this setting. Finally, following Naber--Valtorta (Ann. Math. 185, 2017) and Edelen--Engelstein (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 371, 2019), we prove the nondegenerate set has locally finite $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-measure and is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable.
item.dc:creator: Lili Du, Chunlei Yang, Jing Yang

item.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
item.description:
arXiv:2610.19983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(\Omega)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, using AI, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-\Delta+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.
item.dc:creator: Svitlana Mayboroda, Alberto Pacati

item.title: Volume-dependent geometry and symmetry transitions of torsion optimizers in infinite cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2610.25267v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study relative torsional rigidity in infinite cylinders, addressing two geometric questions raised by Caldiroli, Iacopetti and Pacella on the shape of volume-constrained optimizers. The torsion problem has Dirichlet conditions on the free boundary and Neumann conditions on the fixed lateral wall. At small volumes we establish a two-term expansion of the optimal energy, curvature selection, and quantitative convergence of optimizers to boundary half-balls. We also obtain a uniform expansion for the exact torsion states on the explicit curved half-ball comparison domains. At sufficiently large volumes, every optimizer is exactly a finite cylinder, without convexity of the cross-section or an a priori free-boundary regularity assumption. The normalized optimal value is strictly decreasing up to a finite global transition threshold and constant thereafter. We distinguish this threshold from the local spectral stability threshold and prove coexistence of cylindrical and noncylindrical optimizers when the thresholds are separated. Exact one-sided derivative formulas identify nondifferentiability with the range of transverse energies among optimal states. Strict separation holds for all rectangular cross-sections and for sufficiently close smooth convex inner approximations of any rectangle, with no aspect-ratio restriction. These smooth examples exhibit both curvature-dependent small-volume concentration and a global symmetry transition.
item.dc:creator: Xiuda Liang, Wenjie Wang

item.title: Narrow escape problems beyond spherical holes: slits and tubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The narrow escape problem consists in characterizing the exit event of a Brownian motion trapped inside a domain with reflecting boundary and small absorbing holes. Using recent advances in the quasi-stationary distribution approach, we first give an explicit set of hypotheses that allows one to derive the asymptotics of the exit time and of the exit hole distribution. We then apply it in dimension three to several hole shapes: spherical holes, thin spheroidal holes shrinking to curves on the boundary (slits), and holes located at the end of thin tubes attached to the domain. We illustrate the accuracy of the results with numerical simulations, and extend them to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Louis Carillo

item.title: On some connections between Kobayashi geometry and pluripotential theory
item.description: arXiv:2505.16949v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we explore some connections between Kobayashi geometry and the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation. Among the results we obtain through these connections are: $(i)$~a theorem on the continuous extension up to $\partial{D}$ of a proper holomorphic map $F: D\longrightarrow \Omega$ between domains with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(D) < \dim_{\mathbb{C}}(\Omega)$, and $(ii)$~a result that establishes the existence of bounded domains with ``nice'' boundary geometry on which H\"older regularity of the solutions to the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation fails. The first, a result in Kobayashi geometry, relies upon an auxiliary construction that involves solving the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with H\"older estimates. The second result relies crucially on a bound for the Kobayashi metric.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Bharali, Rumpa Masanta

item.title: Spectral and Schr\"odinger estimates restricted to submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.02012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and smooth bounded geometry. We prove logarithmic spectral projection estimates restricted to uniformly embedded submanifolds. On surfaces with pinched negative curvature, we also prove frequency-independent $L^2\to L^3$ Schr\"odinger restriction estimates on compact geodesic segments for times $c\lambda^{-1}\log\lambda$. If such a surface is even asymptotically hyperbolic, the $L^2\to L^q$ spectral estimates on complete nontrapped geodesics, for $q>2$, gain the square root of the window width. The high-frequency Schr\"odinger estimate holds for all times on these surfaces, both on compact segments and on complete nontrapped geodesics. Under a regularity assumption at the spectral threshold, the all-time estimate holds on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace.
item.dc:creator: Zhexing Zhang

item.title: A mass-type invariant for smooth metric measure spaces and its relation with the fractional Yamabe problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.23248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On asymptotically Schwarzschild smooth metric measure spaces modeled on the Euclidean half-space, we define a new mass-type invariant analogous to the ADM mass of an asymptotically flat manifold. We prove that this invariant is independent of the choice of admissible asymptotic coordinates. We further show that it fits into a very general framework for mass-type invariants and we also isolate static equations for smooth metric measure spaces under natural boundary conditions. For smooth metric measure spaces obtained through a generalized stereographic projection using the Green's function associated with the fractional Yamabe problem, we identify the mass with the constant term in the asymptotic expansion of the Green's function. This identification gives a geometric interpretation of the constant appearing in the fractional Yamabe problem and recasts its conjectured positivity as a positive-mass-type question.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Almaraz, Levi Lopes de Lima, Shaodong Wang

item.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
item.description: arXiv:2609.30209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.
item.dc:creator: Linjun Li, Shihe Liu, Lingfu Zhang
